thread:
sara: heads-up — noticed a 3x jump in p99 token latency on h100 pool after last night's autotune push. correlation looks like sequence-length threshold moved from 48 -> 64 and we started falling back to the CUDA/CUTLASS path for long-ish prompts. anyone else seeing this? :thinking_face:

javier: saw the alert. reproducing locally now with the canonical perf harness. early signs point at KV-cache affinity causing smaller batches and poor kernel utilization when the path flips.

kemal: pv: please paste the perf profiler output if you have it. curious whether it's pure kernel throughput or staging overhead.

sara: paste of a sampling run (repro config: gpt-13b, seq=64, kv_warm=false):
```
[2026-03-18 02:12:10] request_id=abc123 chosen_path=triton_seq_small reason=default
[2026-03-18 02:12:10] chosen_kernel=triton_matmul_fast avg_tok_ms=0.9 p99_kernel_ms=1.2
[2026-03-18 02:12:10] fallback_trigger=seq_threshold_crossed new_path=cuda_cutlass_pref avg_tok_ms=2.9 p99_kernel_ms=4.1
[2026-03-18 02:12:10] kv_cache_state=partially_warm batch_size=2
```
Seems when kv_cache_state!=fully_warm and batch_size<=2 we trigger the CUDA path and p99 spikes.

mia: is this the new heuristic that tries to prefer CUTLASS for seq>=64? we added that because triton was regressing on long seqlen throughput in the earlier sweep.
javier: yes, autotune rule: if estimated_gflops_cutlass > estimated_gflops_triton * 1.05 and seq >= seq_threshold then prefer CUTLASS. seq_threshold changed to 64 in the last rollout. fallback logic also kicks in when kv-affinity indicates low kv-hit -> smaller batches.
randal: quick thought: our estimated_gflops is a static table and doesn't account for batch-smearing/backpressure from KV cache misses. hence when kv cache is cold we should bias toward the lower fixed-overhead kernel (even if peak gflops lower).
kemal: agreed. two possible fixes: 1) make autotune consider effective_batch = batch_size * kv_hit_rate, or 2) add hysteresis so a single sample doesn't switch paths mid-conversation.
ops-bot: deploy checklist note: autotune-config v2.3 promoted at 1767809000 by deploy-bot. previous version was v2.2 pinned to seq_threshold=48.
mia: we should probably rollback seq_threshold to 48 for the h100 pool and run a controlled canary with the kv-aware estimator. I'll open a quick PR to patch the heuristic.
javier: +1. also can we add a lightweight probe that logs `effective_batch` and `kv_hit_rate` to trace so we can verify the metric drives the decision? keep it low-overhead.
sara: repro run with synthetic warm kv (kv_hit_rate ~ 0.95) shows CUTLASS path is faster for throughput-heavy workloads, p99 remains fine. with kv_hit_rate ~ 0.2 p99 explodes on CUTLASS. so it's definitely interaction between kv and kernel.
randal: for the rollback plan: patch autotune -> rollback seq_threshold to 48 for pools [h100-prod,h100-canary], monitor p99 and CPU/GPU util for 2 hours, then re-evaluate with kv-aware estimator. I'll take the rollback.
deploy-bot: scheduled rollback: autotune-config -> v2.2 on pools h100-prod,h100-canary at 1767813000. CI: green.
mia: once rollback is live we'll run overnight batch of the perf harness and capture the tracer logs: we need to quantify how often KV cold starts lead to path flip.
javier: follow-up action items: 1) add `kv_hit_rate` into path scoring model (owner: javier, ETA: 48h), 2) add 5s hysteresis to path switching per request_id (owner: kemal, ETA: 24h), 3) add low-overhead tracer for `effective_batch` (owner: mia, ETA: 24h).
sara: thanks — and please add a small eval case to the regression suite that simulates kv partially warm scenarios (batch=1-3, seq=48-80). we should prevent this from regressing in CI.
randal: I'll monitor p99 via the dashboard and post an update in the morning. tagging @oncall in case rollback has side-effects. :thumbsup:
mia: adding notes to the autotune PR about why static gflops table is insufficient. will include link to the profiler trace.
sara: great. closing loop: rollback + probe + model change. will re-open if we see odd regressions after rollback. thanks all.
